The message came at 7:10 in the evening, from an account with no photo. A video: Chinmay's own face, at what looked like the college canteen, pushing money from the till into his pocket. Then: "Pay 8000 by midnight or this goes to your class group and your parents."
Chinmay had never touched that till. He sat on the floor of his rented room, heart pounding, already opening his banking app.
He called Hemant instead, his older cousin, before he could change his mind.
Hemant arrived in twenty minutes, still in his office shirt. "This is not your fault. Don't pay, don't reply. Screenshot everything: the video, the account, the time."
They reported the account on the app. Then Hemant drove them to the cyber police station.
The sub-inspector noted every detail. "You did right coming today. Paying only brings a bigger demand. We'll file it now and flag the account."
On the drive back, Chinmay finally cried.

They didn't reply to the sender. Diego helped him screenshot everything: the account name, the messages, the time.
